checked_obligation: Under the temporary assumption that a is a primitive root modulo the prime p=4t+3, prove that -a has order (p-1)/2 modulo p.
reason: Let q=(p-1)/2=2t+1. Since a has order p-1, a^q is not congruent to 1; Fermat's theorem and a^{2q}-1=(a^q-1)(a^q+1) therefore give a^q congruent to -1 modulo p. As q is odd, (-a)^q congruent to 1. Conversely, if (-a)^n congruent to 1, then a^{2n} congruent to 1, so p-1 divides 2n and hence q divides n. Thus q is the least positive exponent giving 1, so ord_p(-a)=q. The supplied quotient-group and isomorphism rules are unnecessary.
